challenges.finding: Tshopo contact follow-up is 44.5%, affected by a health-worker strike, aggression and threats. Three of five validated Ituri PoC suspects were not transferred because of ambulance unavailability or refusal. Avakubi is nonfunctional and Butuhe remains closed.
Ituri reports 37 critical patients and insufficient blood. Nord-Kivu has 160 patients outside CTE/CT. Two confirmed patients escaped in Bafwasende.

Nord-Kivu household decontamination is 57.9%, no household kits were provided and 37 safe burials were postponed. Tshopo reports nine of ten bodies not swabbed. Bas-Uele has 16 of 20 priority facilities without functional triage.

Vaccination observations describe research or compassionate activity, not demonstrated BDBV efficacy. Ituri reports 1,873 vaccinated; Bas-Uele reports 1,785 of 13,202 targeted (13.5%). Generator failure stopped PPL vaccination in Haut-Uele.

Continuity assessments report absent triage or emergency services in Oicha facilities. CH Rapha in Nord-Kivu lacks running water, oxygen and blood products. Isiro in Haut-Uele reports a 28-day BCG and syringe stockout.
Ituri psychosocial coverage reaches 15 of 28 affected zones. Pillar case cohorts differ from daily incidence. Support staff in Wanie-Rukula lack training, communications and transport.
Tshopo treatment-centre construction and extension continue, with 115 motorcycles still missing. The Bas-Uele logistics sentence is truncated; no missing project status is inferred.
Only three of eight DPS reported PSEA activities. The reporting mechanism is known in 15 of 36 Ituri zones and four of 34 Nord-Kivu zones. Distinct pillar populations are not added together.
